etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/woru/ → /oru/
From Old Japanese. First attested in the Kojiki of 712 CE in the 連用形 (ren'yōkei, “continuative or stem form”) with the phonetic man'yōgana spelling of 袁理 (⟨wori⟩). Also attested in the Man'yōshū, completed some time after 759 CE.
Listed in some sources as derived from the 連用形 (ren'yōkei, “continuative or stem form”) wi of verb wiru (modern いる (iru)) + ある (aru). The conjugation paradigm for woru is indeed the same as aru for Classical and Old Japanese. However, the resulting compounded *wiaru form would ordinarily become yaru or (w)eru via historical phonetic change, and the vowel shift to /o/ is unexplainable in this hypothesis.
Alternatively, from *wu + ari or *wo + ari, where *wu or *wo is the root of the verb wiru (modern いる (iru), and ari is the Old Japanese form of modern ある (aru).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/ɕikari ɕi/ → /ɕikaɕːi/ → /ɕikaɕi/
Possibly a shift from 然(しか)り (shikari, “being like so”, the 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of classical verb 然(しか)り (shikari, “to be like so”)) + し (shi, the 連体形 (rentaikei, “attributive form”) of past recollective auxiliary き (ki)), contracting from shikari shi to shikasshi, and then further to shikashi.
The initial sense may have been parseable as that [preceding statement] being so, ..., much like English phrases such as be that as it may or that said, followed by a statement in opposition to the earlier statement.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Contraction of どの様(よう)な (dono yō na).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Old Japanese, ultimately from Proto-Japonic *naru. Related to 生(な)る (naru).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Reduplication of 増す (masu).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From もし (moshi, “if”) + も (mo, “also, too, even”, inclusive particle).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: The second component is likely と (to, “with”, explanatory particle for adverbs). The initial component may be a shortening of 漸(ようや)く (yōyaku, “at last, finally, barely”), akin to やく (yaku).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowed from English image, possibly mistaking -age is pronounced /eɪd͡ʒ/, as in page, stage, engage, etc.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Clipping of トイレット (toiretto), borrowed from English toilet.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 初步 (t͡ʃʰɨʌ buoᴴ).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese. First cited to the Nihon Shoki of 720 CE.
Analyzed as a compound of 生す (musu, “to beget”) + 女 (me, “female”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Alternative spelling. See 子 (ko).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/ipa/ → /ifa/ → /iwa/
From Old Japanese. Found in the Man'yōshū finished some time after 759 CE.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 岩 (MC ngaem).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 延 (en, “to extend”) + 長 (chō, “long”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 拡(かく) (kaku, “expand”) + 大(だい) (dai, “big”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Related to 掴(つか)まる (tsukamaru, “to hold oneself still by grabbing something”) and its active form 掴(つか)む (tsukamu, “to grab, to grip, to take hold of”), both originally from 束(つか) (tsuka, “bundle”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: The 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 暮(く)れる (kureru, “to get dark, to end”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 連用形 (“stem form”) of verb 楽しむ (“to enjoy”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 水 (sui, "water," "cold water) + 蒸気 (jōki, "steam," "vapor").

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
⟨nami₁⟩ → /namʲi/ → /nami/
From Old Japanese 浪 (nami₁), from Proto-Japonic *nami.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/pa/ → /ɸa/ → /ha/
From Middle Chinese 波 (MC pa).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Short form of ateji (当(あ)て字(じ)) spelling 波蘭 (Pōrando).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Old Japanese. First attested in the Kojiki of 712 CE. From Proto-Japonic *uku.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese compound 現實 /现实 (henᴴ syit).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 現象 (MC henH zjangX).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From the 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 生(う)まれる (umareru, “to be born”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Phrase consisting of 男 (otoko, “male person, man”) + の (no, appositive particle) + 人 (hito, “person”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese, from Proto-Japonic *sara.
Attested in the Nihon Shoki of 720 CE with the phonetic man'yōgana spelling 娑羅 (sara).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compare 驚(おどろ)く (odoroku, “to surprise”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compare 怯(おび)える (obieru, “to be frightened”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/dauro/ → /dɔːro/ → /doːro/
From Middle Chinese 道路 (daw^X luᴴ). Compare modern Mandarin 道路 (dàolù), Cantonese 道路 (dou⁶ lou⁶).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Literally “west of 逢坂の関 (Ōsaka-no-seki, “tollgate of Ōsaka-yama”)”.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/pone/ → /ɸone/ → /hone/
From Old Japanese, from Proto-Japonic *pənay.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/kapara/ → /kaɸara/ → /kawara/
Probably from Sanskrit कपाल (kapāla, “cup, bowl, skull”). Cognate with 瓦 (kawara, “tile, particularly for roofing or flooring”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Middle Chinese 骨 (MC kwot, “bone”).
The knack sense comes from the idea of the bones as the innermost core or essence of something.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 高(こう)校(こう) (kōkō, “high school”) + 生(せい) (-sei, “student; pupil”).
